Create a new default Blazor Web App.\\n2. Select any render mode:\\n\\u0026gt; - Static SSR\\n\\u0026gt; - Interactive Server\\n\\u0026gt; - Interactive WebAssembly\\n\\u0026gt; - Interactive Auto\\n4. Run the application in Debug mode from Visual Studio.\\n5. Launch using Microsoft Edge.\\n6. Open browser Developer Tools.\\n7. Observe the Console tab.\\n\\n**Actual Result**\\nThe console reports: `Permissions policy violation: unload is not allowed in this document`\\n\\n**Additional Observations**\\n\\n1. Reproducible with CSP disabled.\\n2. Reproducible across all Blazor render modes.\\n3. Appears to originate from localhost:/_vs/browserLink.\\n4. Not observed when running the published application.\\n5. Not observed in Google Chrome.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\nNo application exceptions are thrown.\\n\\nBrowser console output: `Permissions policy violation: unload is not allowed in this document`\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n11.0.100-preview.7.26381.103\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n**Environment**\\n\\n- VS 2026 Insiders [12023.133] professional\\n- Microsoft Edge\\n- Local Debug configuration\\n\\n**Additional Context**\\n\\nThe issue was discovered while validating CSP scenarios, but the behavior reproduces even when CSP is completely disabled, suggesting Browser Link or Visual Studio debugging integration as the source of the console violation rather than ASP.NET Core application code.\\n\\n**Repro Repository**\\n\\nSample App: https://github.com/BharatRamsf3693/BlazorCspValidation/tree/main\\nEvidence: https://github.com/BharatRamsf3693/BlazorCspValidation/tree/main/Evidence\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68678\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"BharatRamsf3693\",\"id\":103921986,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/BharatRamsf3693\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/103921986?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"CONTRIBUTOR\",\"labels\":[\"External\"],\"comments\":2,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-21T07:02:08Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T06:56:24Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2026-08-26T06:56:11Z\",\"closed_by\":\"danroth27\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

(it is triggered by the `@attribute [Authorize(Policy = \\u0026#34;Root\\u0026#34;)]` on the razor page)\\n\\nWhen a client lose connection with the server, the overlay `Attempting to reconnect to the server: N of M` appears:\\n\\n![image](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/22667054/3bc90594-35bc-4c18-b38e-36d049c2c170)\\n\\nWhen the client gains back the connection with the server, the same `Circuit` is maintained successfully and the authorization is validated again.\\n\\nWhen the process of the `IAuthorizationHandler` is very fast, the component will resume with its state successfully: \\n\\n![msedge_qx0mIIpW8p](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/22667054/725966b5-9cdc-4a73-ad34-4b031bb413b7)\\n\\nWhen the process of the `IAuthorizationHandler` is taking too \\u0026#34;long\\u0026#34;, the component will be unloaded, replaced with `Authorizing...` when reconnecting, then after authorization is successful, the component will be reloaded with a brand new state, which leads to losing the data that was on the page before losing connection with the server.\\n\\n![msedge_HSVumEpB7Y](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/22667054/25800601-c24c-4058-b5da-76ac325434dd)\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nIn my opinion, there is multiple expected behavior:\\n\\n- The `Authorizing...` should appear but the other component should keep its state while it is pending for authorization.\\n- The user should be able to prevent the `Authorizing...` from appearing. (Is it not possible already?)\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n1. Configure a simple policy `Root` with a custom requirement\\n2. Implement a `IAuthorizationHandler` with a huge delay on it that `Succeed` your pending custom requirement\\n3. Open your DevTools on your browser \\n4. Open a razor page that has a `@attribute [Authorize(Policy = \\u0026#34;Root\\u0026#34;)]`\\n5. Go offline from your DevTools to lose connection with Blazor Server\\n6. Wait for the \\u0026#34;Attempting to reconnect to the server...\\u0026#34;\\n7. Go online again from your DevTools to make SignalR reconnect successfully to Blazor Server\\n\\nAnd now, with a big delay, you should see the component disappear, having `Authorizing...` appear, then the component reloading with its default state.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\nNo exceptions.\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n8.0.100-rc.1.23455.8\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\nMicrosoft Visual Studio When navigating to `/error`, the Error page is rendered statically on the server, then when the client app starts, overwrites the Error page with the NotFound page content on the client. \\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe default project should demonstrate how to mix server-rendered and client-rendered content properly in the same app. Currently, the default project itself demonstrates mixing the render modes incorrectly.\\n\\nWhile putting `@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]` can be considered a workaround, it is undesirable: the layout of the application itself might still be using WebAssembly for even simple interactivity, like collapsing menus. `ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting` bypasses starting the WebAssembly runtime altogether.\\n\\nPossible solutions:\\n- Mark server-rendered content to persist on the client after client interactive routing kicks in. Possibly a marker attribute on the element, a directive, or an `@attribute` similar to `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute`.\\n- Allow `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute` to actually initialize the WebAssembly app, but leave the components marked with this attribute as-is in the DOM. Consider renaming the attribute if so. This might be easy to do using similar mechanics as seen in `PersistentState`\\n- Allow customizing the `Router`. For example, allow a behavior that lets the router \\u0026#34;keep\\u0026#34; the content as-is when a navigation event occurs, by overriding/passing `OnNavigatingAsync` or similar, or by inheriting from the built-in `Router`.\\n- Allow supplying a custom `Router` altogether. This would also allow multiple additional scenarios if community-built routers were to show up: handling localization in the URL, multiple hierarchic routers, etc.\\n- Allow rendering content on the server and let the client WebAssembly app \\u0026#34;consume\\u0026#34; the rendered static HTML as interactive. This might be a stretch, but for some simple cases, it can work.\\n- Modify/implement a new `RenderMode` that allows server-client handoff.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n`dotnet new blazor --name BlazorSSRCSR --all-interactive --interactivity WebAssembly`\\n`cd BlazorSSRCSR`\\n`dotnet run`\\n\\nNavigate to the created app\\u0026#39;s `/error` endpoint. The endpoint will show the server side error, then after a short time, the client side router overwrites the content with the client side `NotFound` page content.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.100-rc.1.25451.107\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\nThis is NOT the same as similar (possibly slightly related) issues:\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/38128\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/42561\\n\\nNote that there\\u0026#39;s also the implication that if this is done, \\u0026#34;mixing\\u0026#34; render modes across a hierarchy might become possible. The `opener` is from another origin so most operation throws Permission Denied error and I only intend to use it for `postMessage`. However if I pass it to any JS function, Blazor attempts to call `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty` on it and causes the app to crash. This also happens to `iframe`s.\\n\\n\\u0026gt; Blocked a frame with origin \\u0026#34;https://localhost:44357\\u0026#34; from accessing a cross-origin frame.\\n\\n![image](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/6388546/969c3ec6-f21e-4d10-b414-0fe51d8aa37b)\\n\\n```js\\nglobalThis.wasmInterop = new class {\\n\\n    getOpener() {\\n        return globalThis.parent;\\n    }\\n\\n    sendReadyMessage(window, op) {\\n        window.postMessage({\\n            op,\\n        });\\n    }\\n\\n}();\\n```\\n\\n```cs\\n@inject IJSRuntime Js;\\n// ...\\n\\nIJSObjectReference? opener;\\n\\nprotected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()\\n{\\n    opener = await Js.InvokeAsync(\\u0026#34;wasmInterop.getOpener\\u0026#34;);\\n}\\n\\nasync Task SendMessageAsync()\\n{\\n    ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(opener);\\n\\n    // This one is fine\\n    await opener.InvokeVoidAsync(\\u0026#34;postMessage\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;hello\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;*\\u0026#34;);\\n\\n    // This one raises the error\\n    await Js.InvokeVoidAsync(\\u0026#34;wasmInterop.sendReadyMessage\\u0026#34;, opener, \\u0026#34;hello\\u0026#34;);\\n}\\n```\\n\\nInterestingly, invoking the reference directly doesn\\u0026#39;t cause a problem. It only happens when it is a function parameter. I traced the source code back to [this line in `ElementReferenceCapture.ts`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/[REDACTED]/src/Components/Web.JS/src/Rendering/ElementReferenceCapture.ts#LL22C1-L22C1):\\n\\n```ts\\nDotNet.attachReviver((key, value) =\\u0026gt; {\\n  if (value \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; typeof value === \\u0026#39;object\\u0026#39; \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(value, elementRefKey) \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; typeof value[elementRefKey] === \\u0026#39;string\\u0026#39;) {\\n    return getElementByCaptureId(value[elementRefKey]);\\n  } else {\\n    return value;\\n  }\\n});\\n```\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nIdeally `hasOwnProperty` should not be called, or at least Exception should be handled.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nGithub repo for the above code: https://github.com/datvm/BlazorHasOwnPropertyBugDemo, you should run both website, the bug can be seen by running the ASP.NET Core website on the Index page, click \\u0026#34;Send message\\u0026#34; button in the iframe.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n7.0.302\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n_No response_\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48521\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"datvm\",\"id\":6388546,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/datvm\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6388546?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-jsinterop\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2023-05-30T18:27:34Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-08-13T15:30:27Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

[2026-08-27T02:17:13.254Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 5081b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":25153,\"title\":\"Blazor WASM: RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore prevents use of ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath\",\"body\":\"I am building a Blazor WASM application that\\u0026#39;s connected to IdentityServer4.\\n\\nThe template for Single User Accounts provides ```LoginDisplay.razor``` which includes the following line:\\n\\n```\\n\\nAfter getting IdentityServer4 integrated via the following article, I noticed that the ```Register``` link simply redirected back to the Blazor app without any error messages.\\n\\nhttps://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/blazor/security/webassembly/hosted-with-identity-server?view=aspnetcore-3.1\\u0026amp;tabs=visual-studio\\n\\nIt wasn\\u0026#39;t clear what the ```RemoteAuthenticatorView``` was doing, so I dug into the code and came across the following:\\n\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/[REDACTED]/src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs#L356\\n\\nIt\\u0026#39;s clear that ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath``` is being used for the redirect, but there is no documentation describing this. After setting the value to my external identity site ```https://localhost:44312/Identity/Account/Register``` (different site entirely), I was presented with ```Sorry, there\\u0026#39;s nothing at this address.``` in the Blazor app. \\n\\nLooking closer at the above line of code, the ```.PathAndQuery``` piece at the end prevents ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath``` from ever being outside the Blazor app.\\n\\nAs a result, setting ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath``` to ```https://localhost:44312/Identity/Account/Register``` executes a redirect to ```https://localhost:44357/Identity/Account/Register``` (my Blazor app).\\n\\nPlease confirm that this is a bug.\\n\\nEdit: ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteProfilePath``` seems to have the same issue.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/25153\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"hallidev\",\"id\":16142069,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/hallidev\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/16142069?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm\",\"affected-most\",\"severity-minor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-auth\",\"triaged\",\"Pillar: Cloud Integration\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":17,\"+1\":9,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":3,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":3,\"eyes\":2},\"created_at\":\"2020-08-22T17:46:27Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-08-26T13:02:51Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The complete authorization result, including `AuthorizationFailureReason` values, is discarded before rendering.\\n\\nThis prevents applications from displaying meaningful authorization failure messages in Blazor UI.\\n\\nThis proposal updates `AuthorizeViewCore` to preserve the full `AuthorizationResult` and expose authorization failure details through authorization-related template contexts.\\n\\nThe design adds:\\n\\n1. A new `AuthorizationStateWithResult` type that extends `AuthenticationState` and includes `AuthorizationResult`.\\n2. A new `Forbidden` render fragment for authenticated users who fail authorization.\\n3. Updated fallback behavior so `NotAuthorized` can receive an `AuthorizationStateWithResult` instance when authorization fails and `Forbidden` is not supplied.\\n\\nThis addresses both linked issues:\\n\\n- \\n- \\n\\n---\\n\\n## Problem\\n\\nBlazor\\u0026#39;s `AuthorizeViewCore` currently evaluates authorization and renders one of the existing fragments:\\n\\n- `Authorizing`\\n- `Authorized`\\n- `ChildContent`\\n- `NotAuthorized`\\n\\nThe authorization result is reduced to a boolean value:\\n\\n```csharp\\nresult.Succeeded\\n```\\n\\nAs a result, metadata from `AuthorizationResult` is lost.\\n\\nThis is a problem because custom authorization handlers can produce useful failure reasons:\\n\\n```csharp\\ncontext.Fail(\\n    new AuthorizationFailureReason(\\n        this,\\n        \\u0026#34;Missing permission: Project.Read\\u0026#34;));\\n```\\n\\nToday, `AuthorizeView` does not provide a supported way for Razor markup to display that failure reason.\\n\\nThis creates two related gaps.\\n\\n### Gap 1: Authorization Result Is Not Exposed\\n\\nApplications cannot access the following from `AuthorizeView` UI templates:\\n\\n```csharp\\nAuthorizationResult\\nAuthorizationFailure\\nAuthorizationFailureReason\\n```\\n\\nThis prevents applications from showing detailed authorization failure messages.\\n\\n### Gap 2: Authenticated Forbidden Users Are Not Separated from Anonymous Users\\n\\nToday, both anonymous users and authenticated unauthorized users generally flow through `NotAuthorized`.\\n\\nApplications often need different UI:\\n\\n```text\\nAnonymous user:\\nPlease sign in.\\n\\nAuthenticated but unauthorized user:\\nYou are signed in, but you do not have permission.\\n```\\n\\nA dedicated `Forbidden` state gives applications a clearer way to represent the authenticated-but-not-authorized case.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Goals / Non-Goals\\n\\n### Goals\\n\\n1. Preserve the full `AuthorizationResult` returned by `IAuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync`.\\n2. Expose authorization failure reasons to Blazor templates.\\n3. Add a dedicated `Forbidden` render fragment for authenticated-but-not-authorized users.\\n4. Preserve existing `NotAuthorized` source compatibility.\\n5. Allow `NotAuthorized` fallback scenarios to access authorization result information without changing the public `NotAuthorized` property type.\\n6. Preserve existing behavior when applications do not use the new API.\\n7. Keep the design simple for common Razor usage.\\n8. Avoid changing policy evaluation, role evaluation, resource authorization, or authentication behavior.\\n9. Provide a path that satisfies both scenarios: exposing the authorization result and separating forbidden UI from anonymous/not-authorized UI.\\n\\n### Non-Goals\\n\\n1. Do not change authorization policy semantics.\\n2. Do not change authentication behavior.\\n3. Do not remove or rename existing `AuthorizeView` parameters.\\n4. Do not require applications to use `Forbidden`.\\n5. Do not automatically sanitize, localize, or rewrite authorization failure messages.\\n6. Do not introduce a general-purpose diagnostics API for authorization.\\n7. Do not change routing authorization behavior outside the scope of `AuthorizeViewCore`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Detailed Design\\n\\n### Overview\\n\\nThe proposed design changes `AuthorizeViewCore` so that the component stores the full `AuthorizationResult` instead of only storing whether authorization succeeded.\\n\\nThe design introduces a new context type:\\n\\n```csharp\\nAuthorizationStateWithResult\\n```\\n\\nThis type derives from `AuthenticationState` and adds an `AuthorizationResult` property.\\n\\nThe same type is used by:\\n\\n1. `Forbidden`\\n2. `NotAuthorized` fallback scenarios where authorization failed\\n\\nThis design fixes both issues:\\n\\n- `Forbidden` provides a clear, explicit 403-style rendering path for authenticated users who fail authorization.\\n- `NotAuthorized` can still access authorization failure details when `Forbidden` is not supplied.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### New Context Type\\n\\nAdd a new public type:\\n\\n```csharp\\nnamespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization;\\n\\npublic sealed class AuthorizationStateWithResult : AuthenticationState\\n{\\n    public AuthorizationStateWithResult(\\n        ClaimsPrincipal user,\\n        AuthorizationResult authorizationResult)\\n        : base(user)\\n    {\\n        AuthorizationResult = authorizationResult;\\n    }\\n\\n    public AuthorizationResult AuthorizationResult { get; }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Purpose\\n\\n`AuthorizationStateWithResult` represents the current authentication state plus the result of authorization evaluation.\\n\\nIt allows existing `AuthenticationState`-based templates to continue working while providing access to authorization metadata in failed authorization scenarios.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Authorization State Storage\\n\\n`AuthorizeViewCore` should preserve the full authorization result internally.\\n\\nConceptually, instead of storing only whether authorization succeeded, the component stores:\\n\\n```csharp\\nprivate AuthorizationResult? currentAuthorizationResult;\\n```\\n\\nThe `null` state represents that authorization is still in progress.\\n\\nWhen no authorization data applies to the component, the result is treated as successful:\\n\\n```csharp\\ncurrentAuthorizationResult = AuthorizationResult.Success();\\n```\\n\\nWhen authorization data is present, the component stores the full result returned by the authorization service:\\n\\n```csharp\\ncurrentAuthorizationResult =\\n    await AuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync(\\n        user,\\n        Resource,\\n        policy);\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Existing Fragments\\n\\nThe existing fragments remain:\\n\\n```csharp\\nRenderFragment? ChildContent\\nRenderFragment? Authorized\\nRenderFragment? NotAuthorized\\nRenderFragment? Authorizing\\n```\\n\\n### New Fragment\\n\\nAdd:\\n\\n```csharp\\nRenderFragment? Forbidden\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Rendering Behavior\\n\\nThe conceptual rendering behavior is:\\n\\n```csharp\\nif (authorizationResult is null)\\n{\\n    render Authorizing;\\n}\\nelse if (authorizationResult.Succeeded)\\n{\\n    render Authorized or ChildContent with AuthenticationState;\\n}\\nelse\\n{\\n    var stateWithResult = new AuthorizationStateWithResult(\\n        currentAuthenticationState.User,\\n        authorizationResult);\\n\\n    if (currentAuthenticationState.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp;\\n        Forbidden is not null)\\n    {\\n        render Forbidden with stateWithResult;\\n    }\\n    else\\n    {\\n        render NotAuthorized with stateWithResult;\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThis means:\\n\\n- `Forbidden` is preferred for authenticated failed authorization.\\n- `NotAuthorized` remains the fallback path.\\n- Both failed authorization paths can access the full `AuthorizationResult`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Rendering Matrix\\n\\n| Scenario | Rendered Fragment | Context Type |\\n|---|---|---|...

Create a new default Blazor Web App.\\n2. Select any render mode:\\n\\u0026gt; - Static SSR\\n\\u0026gt; - Interactive Server\\n\\u0026gt; - Interactive WebAssembly\\n\\u0026gt; - Interactive Auto\\n4. Run the application in Debug mode from Visual Studio.\\n5. Launch using Microsoft Edge.\\n6. Open browser Developer Tools.\\n7. Observe the Console tab.\\n\\n**Actual Result**\\nThe console reports: `Permissions policy violation: unload is not allowed in this document`\\n\\n**Additional Observations**\\n\\n1. Reproducible with CSP disabled.\\n2. Reproducible across all Blazor render modes.\\n3. Appears to originate from localhost:/_vs/browserLink.\\n4. Not observed when running the published application.\\n5. Not observed in Google Chrome.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\nNo application exceptions are thrown.\\n\\nBrowser console output: `Permissions policy violation: unload is not allowed in this document`\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n11.0.100-preview.7.26381.103\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n**Environment**\\n\\n- VS 2026 Insiders [12023.133] professional\\n- Microsoft Edge\\n- Local Debug configuration\\n\\n**Additional Context**\\n\\nThe issue was discovered while validating CSP scenarios, but the behavior reproduces even when CSP is completely disabled, suggesting Browser Link or Visual Studio debugging integration as the source of the console violation rather than ASP.NET Core application code.\\n\\n**Repro Repository**\\n\\nSample App: https://github.com/BharatRamsf3693/BlazorCspValidation/tree/main\\nEvidence: https://github.com/BharatRamsf3693/BlazorCspValidation/tree/main/Evidence\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68678\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"BharatRamsf3693\",\"id\":103921986,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/BharatRamsf3693\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/103921986?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"CONTRIBUTOR\",\"labels\":[\"External\"],\"comments\":2,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-21T07:02:08Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T06:56:24Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2026-08-26T06:56:11Z\",\"closed_by\":\"danroth27\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The `opener` is from another origin so most operation throws Permission Denied error and I only intend to use it for `postMessage`. However if I pass it to any JS function, Blazor attempts to call `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty` on it and causes the app to crash. This also happens to `iframe`s.\\n\\n\\u0026gt; Blocked a frame with origin \\u0026#34;https://localhost:44357\\u0026#34; from accessing a cross-origin frame.\\n\\n![image](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/6388546/969c3ec6-f21e-4d10-b414-0fe51d8aa37b)\\n\\n```js\\nglobalThis.wasmInterop = new class {\\n\\n    getOpener() {\\n        return globalThis.parent;\\n    }\\n\\n    sendReadyMessage(window, op) {\\n        window.postMessage({\\n            op,\\n        });\\n    }\\n\\n}();\\n```\\n\\n```cs\\n@inject IJSRuntime Js;\\n// ...\\n\\nIJSObjectReference? opener;\\n\\nprotected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()\\n{\\n    opener = await Js.InvokeAsync(\\u0026#34;wasmInterop.getOpener\\u0026#34;);\\n}\\n\\nasync Task SendMessageAsync()\\n{\\n    ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(opener);\\n\\n    // This one is fine\\n    await opener.InvokeVoidAsync(\\u0026#34;postMessage\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;hello\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;*\\u0026#34;);\\n\\n    // This one raises the error\\n    await Js.InvokeVoidAsync(\\u0026#34;wasmInterop.sendReadyMessage\\u0026#34;, opener, \\u0026#34;hello\\u0026#34;);\\n}\\n```\\n\\nInterestingly, invoking the reference directly doesn\\u0026#39;t cause a problem. It only happens when it is a function parameter. With browserlink enabled, a `ScriptInjectionFilterStream` is used instead and `context.Response.HasStarted`, will always be false which will lead to the original exception being thrown at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/[REDACTED]/src/Middleware/Diagnostics/src/ExceptionHandler/ExceptionHandlerMiddlewareImpl.cs#L185\\n\\nPerhaps .NET can start writing to the stream earlier to ensure `context.Response.HasStarted` will be true? \\n\\nThis will have been introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/25288 I believe.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nI\\u0026#39;m expecting a 404 to be returned instead of a 500 error thrown by .NET Core. \\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nTo replicate: \\n1) set up a custom exception handler, something similar to https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling?view=aspnetcore-7.0#produce-a-problemdetails-payload-for-exceptions. \\n2) Instead of `StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError`, use a 404 status code\\n3) Throw an exception on a controller that\\u0026#39;s uncaught which will force the exception handler to run\\n4) Use Postman or any tool to do a request with a request header `Accept: text/html`. This will force browserlink to work and use a `ScriptInjectionFilterStream`.\\n5) An error is now returned instead of the expected 404. \\n6) Turn off browserlink completely and a 404 will be returned as expected\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n.NET 6 and .NET 7\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n_No response_\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/45622\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"stambunan\",\"id\":29392958,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/stambunan\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/29392958?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"CONTRIBUTOR\",\"labels\":[\"External\",\"area-mvc\"],\"comments\":2,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2022-12-16T03:01:49Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2023-01-19T12:00:54Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2022-12-20T10:14:31Z\",\"closed_by\":\"javiercn\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

It\\u0026#39;s not in my app code. (Answer follows)\\n\\nThird, where are these script tags getting injected? They are not in the initial HTML being served to the browser.\\n\\nThe answer to the second and third puzzles is *identity server\\u0026#39;s `/connect/checksession` endpoint*. If you look at the network trace for it:\\n\\n![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1101362/136238297-74e61316-bdb6-4a7d-b5c1-db8dcd761ecf.png)\\n\\nPlus the response headers contain:\\n\\n```\\ncontent-security-policy: default-src \\u0026#39;none\\u0026#39;; script-src \\u0026#39;sha256-fa5rxHhZ799izGRP38+h4ud5QXNT0SFaFlh4eqDumBI=\\u0026#39;\\n```\\n\\n**I\\u0026#39;m pretty sure this cannot be a valid place for us to inject either the Browserlink script or the `aspnetcore-browser-refresh.js` script**, because:\\n\\n1. Why would we do this? Then they only take effect when you\\u0026#39;re logged in. That can\\u0026#39;t be what we want. Also I think they would incorrectly try to reload whatever hidden iframe this file is being loaded into, and who knows what that will lead to.\\n2. The CSP is going to deny them anyway.\\n\\nI\\u0026#39;m not really certain whether either Browserlink or ASP.NET Core hot reload should be present in the SPA templates. Maybe not, in which case somehow removing them would fix all of this. But if they are meant to be there we need to find a different way to inject them.\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/37326\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-mvc\",\"feature-spa\"],\"assignees\":[\"pranavkm\",\"jodavis\"],\"milestone\":\"6.0.0\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2021-10-06T15:50:46Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2021-11-11T18:00:41Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2021-10-12T17:02:29Z\",\"closed_by\":\"pranavkm\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

For creating new items, use create_issue, create_discussion, or create_pull_request instead. IMPORTANT: Comments are subject to validation constraints enforced by the MCP server - maximum 65536 characters for the complete comment (including footer which is added automatically), 10 mentions (@username), and 50 links. Exceeding these limits will result in an immediate error with specific guidance. NOTE: Discussion comments are disabled for this workflow because discussions:write permission is not available. Set 'discussions: true' in the workflow's safe-outputs.add-comment configuration to enable discussion comments and request this permission. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 comment(s) can be added. Target: *. This tool records a real comment intent. Do not use it for placeholder comments, auth checks, or probing. Call it only when the final comment body is ready; otherwise use noop or report_incomplete.

safeoutputs.description: Log a transparency message when no significant actions are needed. This is distinct from noop (no action needed) — it indicates an active failure that prevented the task from running.
